# Lead-only recording kit — not executed by K3a

Use one authorized disposable sandbox per CLI. The lead prepares the subscription
realm/login and launcher; this lane does not inspect any login directory or state.
No installation configuration, admission, real preparation or production raw retention
is involved. `record.mjs` invokes the CLI once through the existing isolated runner,
never runs login/version/help, and never retries a failed recording.

`preparation.mjs` exports the harmless one-tool session. It accepts only the fixed
request, creates one random challenge, freezes P including the challenge, appends
and fsyncs the fixture settlement before release, and reuses the same result for
the same-call replay. It calls no product planner/store/approval/admission. This
fsync is recording-fixture custody, not a product durable receipt or source proof.

The exact system/stdin prompts are exported as `recordingSystem`/`recordingStdin`.
They request an early unframed draft, exactly one `propose_work` preparation call,
then a separate final message with the delivered challenge line + LF + one complete
BrainDraft object. No challenge is in the prompts. A model's obedience is not assumed.
The sample business draft is shape data, not acceptance of a purchase.

Prepare a private input JSON (paths are examples, never account defaults):

```json
{
  "outDir": "/tmp/k3a-codex-once",
  "sandboxConfigDir": "<lead-prepared sandbox login locator>",
  "executable": "<absolute authorized CLI binary>",
  "isolationModule": "<absolute lead sandbox isolation-port module.mjs>",
  "catalogFile": "assets/model-catalog/codex-cli-subscription.json",
  "modelId": "<exact active id selected from that catalog>",
  "cliVersion": "<exact numeric version already verified by the lead>",
  "versionEvidence": "<lead version/binary proof reference>",
  "timeoutMs": 60000
}
```

The isolation module exports `isolation`, the existing `HeadlessIsolation` port
returning a measured `BubblewrapCapability`. Use the sandbox's authorized launcher,
not a host execution fallback. The existing isolated runner alone binds the lead's
sandbox login and gateway. Do not point this kit at an installation's live state.
For Claude select its catalog and a fresh output directory. The model minimum is
checked against registry data; no model/CLI/transport substitution is made.

Run once for each prepared input, under the heavy lock and outside a Vitest run:

```sh
flock /tmp/claude-1000/deckent-heavy.lock node tests/fixtures/same-turn-planning/record.mjs <private-input.json>
```

`nativeAgentLaunch` calls **codexAgentArgv** / **prepareClaudeAgentRun**. The script
prints and records their complete effective argv; it never hand-derives flags.
[argv.from-source.json](argv.from-source.json) was printed by calling those two
producers directly from the lead-built base, with a disposable directory and a
fixture-only bridge credential, without launching a CLI. Its models came from the
first active registry rows; those print examples are not the lead's model selection
or a recording. No partial-message flag or chat max-turns is introduced.

Capture and review both CLI streams in order:

- Codex: thread/turn, early assistant, MCP start/call/args, fixture P settlement and
  release, correlated completed MCP result W, one completed assistant id containing
  challenge + D, turn.completed/usage, process exit/close/drain. No START is invented.
- Claude: init/session/version/model, early assistant, tool_use.id + arguments,
  P settlement/release, equal user.tool_result W, separate top-level final message.id
  with null parent and challenge + D, equal result.result in the same session,
  success/is_error=false/explicit end_turn, exit/close/drain. Result UUID is not a
  message id. Null/unknown stop or text/session/parent disagreement is failure.

The manifest records recording provenance; binary realpath/hash and supplied version
proof; model minimum/catalog revision/hash and flag-set digest; exact argv/digest;
stdin/system digests; raw stdout/stderr hash/bytes/lines; invocation/preparation count;
exit/signal/truncation/limit and egress evidence. `custody.jsonl` binds call/turn/
generation/correlation, argsDigest, token-inclusive P bytes/resultDigest and release.
Actual W remains in captured native stdout. The public manifest never stores the
bridge credential, child environment or private MCP config. Run files are disposed.

Before persisting raw stdout/stderr the kit checks the bridge's known-secret snapshot
and credential/JWT/email patterns. A hit writes only failure metadata, never raw
streams. This heuristic is not a proof that all possible secrets are absent; the lead
must review all files, including custody, before copying/publishing any fixture.
The challenge is fixture evidence, separate from bridge authentication. No production
redaction bypass or raw-retention path is added.

A fresh output directory is the one-shot marker. Nonzero exit, refused startup,
truncation/limit, missing/extra preparation or secret-check failure is reported with
exit 1 and must not be blindly repeated. Exit 0 means capture awaiting protocol
review, not protocol PASS. Missing early draft, delivery correlation, framing, normal
completion or exact D is a failed positive; report it to the lead without retry.

Only after both real wire positives pass review may the lead open K1/K2. K3 later
replays the same D through the real planner/finalizer/source/approval stores: one
receipt/source/card, zero Run before decision, deny/expiry zero, allow one, replay
no new claim/send/card/admission. Crash/unknown and beta.2-reader proof remain open.
Codex's unreported provider truncation remains indistinguishable; challenge does not
establish normal finish, semantic use of preparation or plan correctness.
